reasoning: 3-month-old infant with feeding difficulty (inability to drink bottle) — concerning for upper airway compromise or systemic illness

Tachycardia: HR 132 is at upper normal/mildly elevated for age (normal ~100–160); in context of respiratory findings, raises concern for compensatory response
Dried mucus in both nares + feeding difficulty = potential nasal obstruction impairing infant's ability to feed while breathing (obligate nasal breathers at this age)
No fever (T 98°F/36.7°C), SpO2 99% reassuring against severe pneumonia or sepsis, but does not exclude viral illness, early sepsis, or anatomic obstruction
First-time patient with no prior records — unable to assess for chronic conditions or baseline; increases uncertainty

ESI Handbook guidance: infants with signs of respiratory compromise or feeding problems warrant uptriage; nasal obstruction impairing feeding in a 3-month-old is not trivial
